title: Soft-cutover checkpointed handoff for active-active gateway
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Redwood's hosted API must maintain user-visible streaming/session continuity during partial region degradation (network flaps, partial host pools degrading) while also preserving SLOs and avoiding cascading overload in healthy regions. Current hard cutovers cause stream resets and client-visible glitches. We need an active-active approach that performs soft cutovers with checkpointed handoff for in-flight streaming sessions and robust load-shedding / circuit-breaker behavior for new traffic targeting a degraded region.

Goals:
- Preserve per-customer SLOs: streaming 95/99 latency and completion rate targets; page in acceptance criteria.
- Avoid routing storms: ensure healthy region capacity isn't overwhelmed during failover.
- Minimize client-side reconnects for streaming sessions when we shift traffic.
- Maintain observability for post-mortem and gradual rollout.

Proposed design (summary):
1) Soft cutover semantics: instead of draining immediately, edge gateways mark a region as "soft-draining" and annotate sessions with a checkpoint token (opaque checkpoint ID stored in global KV) and a per-session handoff TTL. New requests continue to route normally until routing policy begins gradual traffic weighting away from the region.
2) Checkpointed handoff for streams: every N tokens (configurable, default 512) the serving runtime writes a compact session checkpoint into the global KV (session manifest: last processed input offset, minimal decoder KV-cache digest, model variant). Checkpoints are versioned and small (~1-4KB). On attempt to rehydrate in the peer region, the runtime pulls the latest checkpoint and resumes generation with the cached KV digest + model warmups.
3) In-flight RPC fallback: if checkpoint is stale or missing, consumer attempts a short replay strategy: client re-issues the last few messages and we replay into a fresh KV to reach a consistent state (we document limits and possible content regression).
4) Load-shedding and circuit-breakers: per-region circuit-breakers trip based on steady-state metrics (5xx rate, 95p latency, queue depth) and emit a region-degraded flag. When a region is degraded, routing controller moves traffic incrementally (soft weight drain: 10% steps every 30s) and enforces per-customer concurrency caps and token-bucket rate limits. If the target region is under pressure during failover, we apply prioritized shedding: reject new low-priority requests (background embeddings, low-tier customers) before high-priority streaming sessions.
5) Streaming handshake token: to avoid mid-stream duplication clients attach a handshake header with current checkpoint ID; receiving region verifies the checkpoint and either accepts a resume or requests a short replay.
6) Observability: expose checkpointing frequency, checkpoint size, KV get/put latencies, resume success rate, and per-request resume path as first-class Grafana panels and SLO-driven alerts.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Checkpointing every token would be too expensive: we sweep at a configurable interval (token count + time window) to balance cost and resume fidelity.
- Global KV adds cross-region read/write dependency; we mitigate by making checkpoints small and caching them at the edge with short TTL to avoid thundering reads.
- Perfect mid-stream resume is impossible for some workloads (non-deterministic sampling, external tool calls); we surface failure modes clearly to clients and provide best-effort resume with retriable semantics.

Rollout plan:
- Spike + unit tests (done) -> internal alpha in canary region (2 weeks) -> limited partner beta for a subset of customers (4 weeks) -> gradual account-wide rollout with telemetry gating (SLO pass) -> GA.

Testing & validation:
- Fault injection harness to simulate partial region flaps and network partitions.
- Chaos experiments with synthetic streaming loads and mix of high/low priority traffic.
- E2E resume validation across models (causal/text-streaming + chat multi-turn) and quantized variants.

Open questions / next actions:
- Checkpoint schema finalization: reduce to minimal KV digest vs full kv-store snapshot. Action: research spike to quantify resume latency overhead (Miguel).
- Pricing implications for KV storage and cross-region egress billing; loop in finance.
- Client SDK changes for handshake header and replay strategies; coordinate with devx.

Acceptance criteria:
- Streaming resume success >= 95% for canonical chat workloads during soft-cutover in canary.
- No P0 SLO breaches in healthy region during cutover (defined as 99p latency and error budgets).
- Dashboards for checkpoint health, resume success, KV latencies, and circuit-breaker events.
- Automated e2e test coverage covering resume and replay path.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Resume success >= 95% on canonical chat streaming workloads in canary. 2) No new P0 SLO breaches in healthy region during progressive traffic shift. 3) Circuit-breaker thresholds documented and implemented; automated tests verifying shedding priority. 4) Dashboards and alerts live in Grafana; runbook updated.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Spike completed: prototype checkpoint writes at 512-token cadence. Observed median checkpoint write 6ms, 99p 25ms to global KV (canary region).
2026-03-04 - Design review with PM (Lena Hoffman) and DevX (Kara Liu). Decided to prioritize minimal KV digest to reduce egress. PM asked to include customer-facing SDK retries doc before beta.
2026-03-06 - Load-shedding thresholds proposed: queue depth > 2500 or 95p latency > 2.5s trips regional circuit. Adding per-customer concurrency caps (default 4).
2026-03-08 - Miguel implemented resume handshake header; integration tests passing locally. Need infra approval for increased KV throughput quota. Filed infra ticket INF-9123.
2026-03-10 - Canary deployment scheduled. Will monitor resume_success, checkpoint_put_errors, cross-region-kv-egress, and region-circuit events.
